atAGlance: Lẩu cá lóc is snakehead fish hot pot, usually with sour broth, elephant ear stem or herbs, noodles, and fish.
whatItIs: Lẩu cá lóc is snakehead fish hot pot with sour broth, herbs, greens, tomatoes, pineapple or tamarind, and noodles. It is a shared fish-table meal.
howToEnjoy: Cook fish pieces carefully, watch for bones, then add greens and noodles in stages. Taste the sour broth before adding chili.
howLocalsOrder: Order lẩu cá lóc by table size. Ask about bones, less spicy broth, or extra herbs before the pot starts bubbling.
worthKnowing: Cá lóc is snakehead fish, common in southern cooking and often paired with sour broths and fresh herbs.
goodToKnow: Ask about bones before ordering if you prefer easy fish pieces. Add greens and noodles after the fish flavors the sour broth.
